purpose: Use Toast for a short confirmation after an action that disappears on its own; a persistent message on a page or section (a banner, a notice) is an Alert. A transient, non-blocking notification system: mount the `<Toaster>` region **once** near the application root, then raise notifications imperatively from anywhere via the exported `toast()` function (`toast('Saved')`) and its type shortcuts (`toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.info`, `toast.warning`, `toast.loading`, `toast.progress`, `toast.promise`, `toast.dismiss`). Each notification is a self-dismissing card that stacks in a corner, animates in and out, and is announced to assistive technology — without stealing focus. Unlike the sibling [`Alert`](./alert.md), which is an **inline** banner the consumer places in the document flow and controls with `v-model`-style props, Toast is a **transient overlay** stack driven by an imperative call and a shared reactive store, so the call site needs no local visibility state and no markup of its own. The card surface, typography, and severity icons follow the Figma design (see `figma` in the frontmatter). The interaction model follows the established mount-once toast pattern (a single anchored region + imperative trigger + auto-dismiss stack that groups collapsed and expands on hover), built on our tokens, our semantic animation utilities, and our composition/compound-API conventions per [`contributing/rules/migration.md`](../contributing/rules/migration.md); nothing is inherited from any external library. Each severity tints only its leading **icon** via the matching `-contrast` token (`var(--success-foreground)` / `var(--warning-foreground)` / `var(--danger-foreground)` / `var(--info-foreground)`) over the shared `var(--bg-surface-raised)` surface.
useWhen: Confirming the result of an action that finished out of view or in the background: saved, deployed, copied.
Following an async operation from start to finish with `toast.promise`, or `toast.loading` plus a dismiss by id.
Following an operation whose completion is known (an upload, an import, a migration) with `toast.progress`: a bar and its percentage, updated in place by id, with a Cancel action.
A short notice that is not tied to one place on the page and can disappear on its own.
avoidWhen: The message must stay visible next to the content it concerns → use `alert`.
The user must decide something before continuing → use `dialog`.
Validation feedback for a single field → use `field-error`.
related: `alert` — inline severity banner placed in the page flow; it stays until it is closed.
`dialog` — blocking modal for decisions and confirmations.
`progress` — rendered under the copy of a `toast.progress` toast.
bestPractices: Mount `Toaster` once at the app root (in `App.vue`, before the layout or `RouterView`), or install `ToastPlugin`. Never render a `Toaster` in a page, a view or a page-body block: only the first `Toaster` to mount is active and it gives the role up when it unmounts, so a page's copy is either inert or, when it mounted first, silences every toast in the app once the user leaves that page. A page only imports `toast`. A full page routed outside the console layout is still a route of the same app, not a root. `check:blocks` fails a block outside `blocks/shells/` that renders one.

Leave the stack at the default `bottom-end` corner (bottom right in a left-to-right page, bottom left in right-to-left). It is the corner a reader reaches last, so a toast never covers the page title, the navigation, the primary action or the text being read, and every Azion app, the docs site included, puts toasts in the same place so the user learns where to look. Don't set `position` on the `Toaster` or the plugin to move the whole stack; a single toast may take another corner only when it must sit next to what it reports.

Use the typed shortcuts (`toast.success`, `toast.error`, …). The type sets the icon and how it is announced: `toast.error` (severity `danger`) interrupts the screen reader through the Toaster's assertive live region, every other type waits its turn in the polite one. Both regions are fixed, so no region ever switches between polite and assertive (switching made screen readers drop or repeat the stack).

Keep the message text to one line and move detail to `description`. Offer at most two actions: one `action`, or `actions` with two entries when a failure has two ways forward (**Edit** and **Redeploy**).
A toast with an `action` (or `actions`) stays at least 10 s unless it sets its own `duration`, so a keyboard or screen-reader user has time to reach the action.
`duration: 0` keeps a toast until it is dismissed. Keep the returned id and call `toast.dismiss(id)`, or pass the same `id` to update the toast in place.

Use `toast.progress(message, value, { id })` when the percentage is known; keep calling it with the same `id` as the value moves (the card updates in place, no new announcement per step), and finish with `toast.success` or `toast.error` on that `id`. Use `toast.loading` when it is not known. Give a long operation a Cancel `action`.
Don't make a toast the only path to an important action. It auto-dismisses and never takes focus.
